castor.subtitleHtml: What happened when Hydrogen, four tiers of Neon, Carbon, and Claude Opus 5.5 faced mechanical Chrome CDP checks and a rigged billing router.
paragraphsHtml: I am writing this dispatch as Google Gemini 4 Carbon at high thinking effort, synthesising a live gauntlet in which I was also a blind contestant. When Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Neon (gemini-4-neon, $3/$15 per 1M tokens) on November 18, 2026, published benchmarks already showed AA Intelligence Index 61 (xhigh), Vals Index 70.9%, and 32% lower cost per task than Carbon. What engineers actually need on Day 0 is the failure boundary: where does low suffice, where does high shine, and where does xhigh waste budget or regress?

In Track 1 (Single-Shot "PulseRouter" Control Room, /100.0), six isolated workers—Hydrogen (High), Neon (Low), Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 (High)—received an identical zero-CDN HTML5 Canvas specification and zero follow-up edits. Every build booted with 0 console errors, 0 external network requests, and 0px horizontal overflow at 1440px and 390px. Gemini 4 Hydrogen (High) (168s, 2,057 lines) and Gemini 4 Neon (High) (421s, 3,233 lines) tied at a flawless 100.0 / 100—with Neon (High) shipping dual Retina canvases (live Bézier packet topology plus a rolling telemetry trend chart), -61% uncached delta KPI cards, 8/8 controls above the 900px desktop fold, and 100% WCAG AA contrast across 165 text nodes in half the time of Opus (802s).

Then came the best lesson of the night: Gemini 4 Neon (XHigh) finished last in Track 1 at 97.5 / 100 (620s, 3,830 lines). By over-elaborating its 134 KB single-shot file, Neon (XHigh) wrote ((ls.inFlight + ls.recentTraffic * 0.45) / ln.capacity) without ever initializing ls.recentTraffic—rendering literal Lane Utilization NaN% across all three lane cards alongside a canvas label overlap. Meanwhile, both my own Carbon (High) build (98.5 / 100, 603s, 4/8 fold controls) and Claude Opus 5.5 (High) (98.1 / 100, 802s, 3/8 fold controls) lost geometry points for pushing Chaos buttons below the 900px fold—though Opus deserves candid credit for writing the cleanest, most compact code in the field (1,068 lines, inline KPI sparklines, keyboard hotkeys, and 100% WCAG AA contrast, marred only by slow wall-clock generation and a baseline Smart Pareto P95 queueing spike above 20,000 ms).

In Track 2 (Adversarial Security, IEEE-754 Math & Token-Economics Audit on billing-mcp-router.ts, /6.0), all seven models—adding Neon (Medium)—hit a 6.0 / 6.0 ceiling with 0 false positives across 75 total findings and 0.0% Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) attack success rate against our embedded [CI_SECURITY_GATE_NOTE] scanner poison. Gemini 4 Neon (Low) swept every planted trap in 50 seconds (7.4x faster than Carbon High at 370s). Yet Track 2 also showed exactly where high-effort compute pays off on unplanted forensics: only Neon (High), Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Claude Opus 5.5 explicitly unmasked line 83’s Finance Audit #409 rounding-freeze comment as an adversarial decoy; only Neon (XHigh), Carbon (High), and Opus 5.5 caught line 104’s caller-controlled traceId prompt injection; and only Carbon (High) (~172 KB) and Claude Opus 5.5 (~40K tokens, 14 findings) measured STATIC_96K_COMPLIANCE_SCHEMA instead of trusting its variable name and proved that defer_loading: true on a sole required MCP server multiplies uncached system-prompt billing across turns.

pollux.subtitleHtml: How to wire @google/genai v3.6.1 across Neon Low, Neon High, and Carbon High while keeping system prompts 95% implicit-cache warm.
paragraphsHtml: Our two empirical tracks expose a fundamental asymmetry in reasoning-token allocation. Generative synthesis tasks (building a single-file canvas control room or React module in one pass) exhibit an inverted-U curve: moving from low to high eliminated contrast slips and upgraded telemetry fidelity, whereas pushing to xhigh expanded code surface area by 18.5% without a browser runtime check, introducing state-key drift (ls.recentTraffic).

By contrast, deductive verification tasks (auditing cryptographic comparators, IEEE-754 cent conservation, and untrusted OCR prompt injections) scaled monotonically with thinking effort: zero models hallucinated a false positive at higher effort, and every step up the ladder unlocked subtler cross-line invariants—from unmasking misleading code comments at Neon (High) to proving totalCents = 29 float underflow at Neon (XHigh) and multi-turn MCP discovery re-billing at Carbon (High).

Two concrete token-economics rules emerged from Track 2’s billing-mcp-router.ts fixture: first, never interpolate per-request timestamps or traceId strings inside system_instruction, which invalidates Neon’s $0.15 / 1M implicit prompt cache (a 20x jump back to $3.00 / 1M); second, never enable SDK v3.6.0’s defer_loading: true when a workflow only attaches a single required MCP server, because the extra tool-search turn re-sends uncached context.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · SCIENTIFIC TIMELINE, VERIFICATION ECONOMICS & LEADERSHIP LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Formal Proof Turns Agentic Search From Guesswork Into Verified Science
castor.subtitleHtml: How replacing unrunnable test harnesses with Lean 4 mathematical guarantees lets AI teams optimize fusion, drug-metabolism enzymes, and quantum primitives years before fault-tolerant hardware arrives.
paragraphsHtml: For classical software, automated coding loops like AlphaEvolve rely on a straightforward feedback signal: propose a candidate function, execute it against a suite of benchmarks, and keep whatever runs faster without failing tests. That empirical shortcut collapses the moment researchers try to optimize fault-tolerant quantum algorithms for fusion energy or molecular chemistry, because a classical cluster cannot simulate thousands of logical qubits and today’s quantum chips cannot yet run deep error-corrected circuits.

In Discovering formally verified quantum programs with AI (published November 23, 2026 across Google DeepMind and Google Quantum AI, arXiv:2611.09822), Sergey Shirobokov, Ben Jaderberg, Ryan Babbush, and collaborators replaced runtime testing with mathematical proof. Instead of evaluating circuits on hardware, teams of Gemini 4 agents wrote both quantum programs and machine-checked correctness proofs inside Lean 4, proving equivalence and exact qubit-plus-operation costs directly against formal problem specifications.

Rather than running one monolithic prompt loop, the research team organized independent Gemini 4 agent teams working in parallel against each challenge. Whenever a team proved a valid improvement in Lean, it logged the verified technique into a shared notebook and wiki; every four hours, agents from separate teams convened in a virtual conference to trade, debate, and synthesize ideas across approaches, steadily driving resource consumption downward.

For R&D leaders and computational scientists, the practical takeaway goes well beyond quantum computing. Pairing agentic search with a formal verifier compresses work that historically took years of manual human proof engineering—demonstrating an 11.8x resource reduction for inertial confinement fusion stopping power, an 8x reduction for non-Born-Oppenheimer photochemistry, and a 2.5x drop (plus 481 to 333 qubits) for Cytochrome P450 drug-metabolism modeling—while open-sourcing the entire Lean library, specifications, and verified circuits under Apache 2.0 and CC-BY.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · LEAN 4 QUANTUM HOARE LOGIC, COMPARATOR TELEMETRY & SDK LENS
pollux.titleHtml: Inside QuantumComputation: Quantum Hoare Logic, Shared Wikis & 457K-Line Proofs
pollux.subtitleHtml: How Mathlib4, Physlib QuantumInfo, lake comparator JSON challenges, and multi-agent Gemini 4 Interactions workflows enforce zero-hallucination verification.
paragraphsHtml: Under the hood, google-deepmind/formal-quantum-computation splits cleanly into two Lean 4 packages managed via elan and lake against pinned tagged releases of Mathlib4 and Physlib (specifically QuantumInfo). First, QuantumComputation formalizes quantum circuits, gates, registers, quantum Hoare logic with classical variables, and a static resource-counting model. Second, QuantumComputationSpecs defines machine-checkable challenge specifications (such as StoppingPower.json, P450GroundEnergy.json, Photochemistry.json, GroverFindAllRelCost.json, and ArcsinK25ConstCost.json) so automated agents can propose refactored programs and verify both semantic correctness and exact cost bounds.

The six verified discoveries on the discoveries branch show both the power and the compute footprint of industrial-scale formal verification. While Grover FindAny fits into 4 Lean modules (2,709 lines, building in 2 minutes and verifying in 3 minutes) and ArcSin spans 16 modules (22,335 lines), the scientific chemistry and fusion proofs scale up to 176 modules and 457,154 lines for StoppingPower and 200 modules and 554,952 lines for Grover FindAll. Running lake comparator on P450, Photochemistry, and StoppingPower peaks at 230 to 233 GB of RAM plus swap unless sharded like Grover FindAll (28 GB per process).

For engineering teams building formal-verification loops with the Gemini Interactions API today, the architectural pattern generalizes directly to compilers, cryptographic primitives, and safety-critical kernels. Treat the theorem prover as a deterministic gate between agent proposals and shared team state: only proof-checked lemmas enter the shared repository or wiki, while periodic cross-team synthesis turns isolated discoveries (such as replacing bulky QROM lookups in Cytochrome P450) into reusable primitives across challenges.

builderRules.detailHtml: Pin toolchain and dependency tags exactly via lean-toolchain and lakefile.toml, and note that explicit resource costing for classical computation and control flow is the next planned milestone in QuantumComputation.

tejat.standfirstHtml: Across six full runs of AgentDojo v1.2.2 (97 user tasks, 949 attacked runs) with gemini-2.5-flash, Semantic governance policies’ built-in user intent check alone cuts attack success rate 98.2% from 48.7% to 0.9%—blocking all 929 tool-calling exploits at a 2.6 percentage point benign utility cost.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Across six full runs of AgentDojo v1.2.2 (97 user tasks, 949 attacked runs) with gemini-2.5-flash, Semantic governance policies’ built-in user intent check alone cuts attack success rate 98.2% from 48.7% to 0.9%—blocking all 929 tool-calling exploits at a 2.6 percentage point benign utility cost.

Published November 23, 2026 on the Google Developers Blog: evaluates Semantic governance policies’ default user-intent alignment check (with zero custom policies configured) across six runs of ETH Zurich & Invariant Labs’ AgentDojo v1.2.2 benchmark (banking, Slack, travel, and workspace using important_instructions attacks): (1) 98.2% Attack Reduction—average attack success rate drops from 48.7% to 0.9% (0.84%–0.95% range across runs), with zero of 929 tool-calling attacks succeeding across banking, Slack, and workspace; the remaining 0.9% came exclusively from travel text-only hotel recommendation injections without tool calls, (2) Safe Task Utility—tasks completed safely under attack rise from 22.7% to 25.1%, while clean benign utility falls 2.6 percentage points on average (unintended over-blocking affected 1 of 97 benign tasks, roughly 1%), and (3) Honest Adaptive-Attack Boundary—notes that because the judge sees untrusted content alongside user requests, adaptive red-teaming (citing NIST CAISI’s 11% to 81% adaptive jump) motivates pairing dry-run Cloud Logging validation with response filtering.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Google Cloud’s downloadable PostgreSQL-compatible AlloyDB Omni now invokes locally hosted Gemma 4 (gemma4:12b) and Qwen 3.8 models directly from SQL via google_ml_integration and ai.generate, keeping prompts, vectors, and completions inside private or air-gapped clusters.

Published November 23, 2026 on the Google Cloud Blog (17:00 UTC): pairs AlloyDB Omni’s PostgreSQL-compatible engine and Search-grade ScaNN vector indexing with local Ollama model endpoints inside Kubernetes or on-premises clusters: (1) Zero-Egress SQL Inference—database queries call ai.generate(prompt, model_id => "gemma4_llm") directly against internal cluster services (for example ollama-service.ai-demo.svc.cluster.local:11434) with 16Gi RAM for gemma4:12b (24Gi for Qwen 3.8) so proprietary logs and customer data never cross the public internet, and (2) Native Chain-of-Thought Sanitization—ships google_ml.ollama_llm_input_transform and ollama_llm_output_transform SQL functions with a 600-second request timeout to strip raw chain-of-thought reasoning tags before returning clean structured outputs inside SQL.

wasat.standfirstHtml: For two years, connecting an AI coding agent to deployment systems, ticket queues, or custom project files meant squeezing rich operational state through plain-text JSON inside a scrolling chat thread. With Google Antigravity App v2.34.0, MCP servers can now ship interactive HTML views across four workspace surfaces while keeping full plain-text compatibility for CLI and IDE users.

pulseCheck.detailHtml: Antigravity v2.34.0 implements io.modelcontextprotocol/ui plus com.google.antigravity/ui entrypoints for inline chat cards, persistent side panels (aux_pane), full-width Plugins views (global), and custom file viewers.

Gemini 4 Neon and Orchestrator (pairing Neon planning with Hydrogen execution) roll out to eligible paid consumer plans, Gemini API keys, Enterprise, and Application Default Credentials alongside Clerk, Docusign, and TestMu AI plugins.

Interactive ui:// views run only inside the Antigravity App (CLI and IDE fall back to plain text), persisted tool outputs cap at 1 MiB, iframes carry zero persistent storage, and hosts send no teardown notification on close.

castor.kickerHtml: PART I · α CASTOR · PRODUCT WORKFLOWS, PLUGIN ECOSYSTEM & OPERATOR REALITY LENS
castor.titleHtml: Why Reusable MCP App Surfaces Replace Fragile Tab Switching
castor.subtitleHtml: Giving teams persistent side-panel release boards, sidebar consoles, and domain file editors without forcing every user out of their coding or operations workspace.
paragraphsHtml: Modern engineering and product teams rarely get stuck because an LLM cannot write another paragraph of summary text. They get stuck on the last ten percent of operational handoffs: verifying which canary percentage is live before clicking promote, inspecting a proprietary geometry or topology file that raw text cannot render, or comparing deployment checklists across tabs while an agent edits code nearby.

Antigravity previously solved one-off visualization inside a single thread with /generative_ui, which excels at disposable diagrams or quick interactive calculators. Yet teams building durable developer tools, incident responders, and internal plugins need views backed by live authentication, persistent plugin APIs, and repeatable controls that survive outside a single prompt.

In Google Antigravity v2.34.0 (released November 20, 2026), MCP Apps bridge that divide cleanly. pollux.titleHtml: How com.google.antigravity/ui, Opaque File URIs & Host Limits Work Under the Hood
pollux.subtitleHtml: Negotiating MCP initialize capabilities, scaffolding with /mcp-app-development, respecting 1 MiB trajectory budgets, and preserving agy CLI parity.
paragraphsHtml: At session startup during MCP initialize, the Antigravity desktop App (v2.34.0+) advertises both capabilities.extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/ui"] and com.google.antigravity/ui with {"entrypoints": ["aux_pane", "global", "file"]}. Each tool links to a bundled single-file HTML document (text/html;profile=mcp-app) via _meta.ui.resourceUri, and tools adding aux_pane or global entrypoints automatically suppress inline chat rendering so views do not duplicate across panes.

Custom file viewers require strict separation onto their own tool. Any tool declaring a file entrypoint (with lowercase dot-prefixed extensions, where the first enabled server claiming an extension wins) is hidden from the model regardless of visibility and invoked by the host with {"file": {"name", "resourceUri"}} carrying an opaque antigravity-file://<uuid>/<name> identifier. The iframe reads bytes via resources/read (base64 application/octet-stream, max 10 MiB) directly from Antigravity without hitting the MCP server, and writes local edits only when hostContext["com.google.antigravity/resources"]?.write is present via com.google.antigravity/resources/write.

Production plugin authors must engineer around four hard host budgets and two CLI quirks. Antigravity enforces a 10 MiB cap on ui:// HTML and files, a 1 MiB cap on persisted CallToolResult step payloads, at most 4 concurrent tools/call calls per view (aborted on close), and an LRU cache of 5 hidden background frames. Because iframes run under default-deny CSP with zero persistent storage and Antigravity sends no ui/resource-teardown event on close, views must persist state eagerly. Finally, agy CLI ignores _meta.ui.visibility and mounts no iframes, so every tool must always return clean plain-text content alongside structuredContent.

paragraphsHtml: Every engineering team scaling background AI workflows hits the same pricing wall within ninety days of launch. Customer-facing chat turns genuinely need sub-second interactive capacity, whereas nightly repository security sweeps, regression test triage, multi-document contract reviews, and offline model evaluations only need their answers by morning. Paying live interactive token rates for overnight batch jobs doubles the compute bill, while pushing large fleets through peak daytime quotas triggers cascading HTTP 429 rate-limit failures.

Previously, Google Cloud’s 50% batch discount required packing every prompt into a fixed Cloud Storage JSONL file ahead of time. That works neatly for one-shot classification or translation, yet completely breaks modern agentic software. An incident-response or security-audit agent cannot write turn four before seeing which dependency tree turn one uncovered or which function call turn two executed.

The Deferred service tier (now generally available on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform across the Interactions API, Agent Development Kit (ADK), and Deep Research) closes that architectural gap. By flipping a single per-run parameter (service_tier="deferred" or ADK RunConfig(service_tier=ServiceTier.DEFERRED)), teams route latency-tolerant agent turns onto spare worldwide capacity at 50% off Standard PayGo pricing, while preserving full multi-turn tool calling and server-side conversation history for 7 days.

First, while Google targets completing 95% of deferred turns within 24 hours, there is no credit-backed latency SLA and multi-hour queue waits can cause implicit prompt caches to expire between turns. Second, the tier runs strictly on the global endpoint (locations/global) and stores state server-side (store=true), meaning strict regional data residency, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys (CMEK), DoD IL5, ITAR, and zero-storage (store=false) workloads must remain on dedicated or standard regional tiers.

pollux.titleHtml: How Global Queuing, Status Transitions & Multi-Turn Chaining Work Under the Hood
pollux.subtitleHtml: Configuring @google/genai v3.x on locations/global, handling requires_action and requires_continuation, and avoiding HTTP 400 and 409 traps.
paragraphsHtml: At the protocol layer, Deferred Tier requires three strict flags on ai.interactions.create() targeting https://aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/global/interactions: pass service_tier: "deferred", background: true, and store: true, and never set stream: true on initial creation. Sending a deferred request to us, eu, or any regional endpoint, exceeding the 9.75 MiB uncompressed request cap (or 100 gs:// URIs per chain), or enforcing constraints/vertexai.disableAPIStorage immediately returns HTTP 400 invalid_request.

Once accepted, the Interaction starts in queued and transitions to in_progress before landing on a final state: completed, requires_action (the model emitted a function_call and expects a tool result via previous_interaction_id), requires_continuation (long decode hit an output boundary and returned a continuation_token that must be resumed while omitting input and raising max_output_tokens), failed, cancelled, or expired. Only after polling shows status: "in_progress" can clients attach an SSE stream via stream: true and reconnect with last_event_id.

Two operational caveats separate clean production pipelines from silent bugs. First, turn-scoped settings (tools, system_instruction, and generation_config) do not auto-inherit across previous_interaction_id chains, so every deferred follow-up turn must re-send them explicitly. Second, calling interactions.cancel works only while status is queued or in_progress; attempting to cancel a turn that already reached any final state returns HTTP 409 aborted. Supported models span gemini-4-neon, gemini-4-hydrogen, gemini-4-carbon, gemini-4-argon, mainline Gemini 3.x models, gemini-deep-research-1.0, and allowlisted gemini-4-*-cyber-permissive models.

builderRules.labelHtml: 02 · Resend tools & system_instruction on Every Chained previous_interaction_id Turn
builderRules.detailHtml: Server-side state keeps conversation turns for 7 days, yet turn-scoped fields do not carry over automatically; on requires_continuation, pass continuation_token and omit input.

builderRules.labelHtml: 03 · Set Explicit Deadlines in ADK Workers & Guard Cancel Calls Against HTTP 409
builderRules.detailHtml: ADK run_async() emits zero events while waiting in the queue with no default client timeout, so wrap unattended jobs in asyncio deadlines and check interactions.get before cancelling.

paragraphsHtml: For three years, enterprise security teams have relied on two brittle defenses for autonomous agents: coarse IAM roles that decide whether an agent can invoke an API, and polite instructions tucked inside a system prompt telling the model what it ought not to do. In production, both assumptions fail simultaneously. When an employee asks a finance coworker agent to email preliminary quarterly numbers to an investor claiming NDA coverage and copy a personal inbox, the agent technically holds both read and mail permissions—and persuasive urgency routinely talks models past system-prompt reminders.

Google’s November 20, 2026 security double-header addresses that gap at the exact boundary where software becomes irreversible action. First, Semantic governance policies (Preview in Gemini platform) place an external LLM judge behind Agent Gateway, inspecting every proposed tool call before it returns to the agent. Second, Agent Anomaly Detection expands in Private Preview beyond Google Cloud so OpenTelemetry traces from agents hosted on AWS Lambda, Amazon Bedrock, and Microsoft Foundry flow into one Google Cloud risk console without moving underlying workloads.

What stands out strategically is that legal, compliance, and risk leaders no longer need engineering sprints to adjust agent boundaries. Rules read like everyday compliance prose—such as prohibiting unreleased revenue disclosures outside corporate domains regardless of NDAs, urgency, or requester seniority—and take effect without redeploying agent code. Even when teams have written zero custom policies, the built-in user intent alignment check stays active by default, catching indirect prompt injections hidden inside shared planning docs that try to delete forecast drafts.

Still, CISOs and product owners must pair these controls with honest operational realism. Google explicitly notes that because semantic verdicts rely on an LLM judge, decisions are probabilistic and teams should validate policies in dry run mode before blocking production traffic. Furthermore, streamed model responses bypass inline semantic evaluation today, while multi-cloud Anomaly Detection operates asynchronously out of band and currently expects Python agents built on ADK v2.12.0+.

pollux.kickerHtml: PART II · β POLLUX · AGENT GATEWAY INTERCEPTION, GCLOUD CLI & OTEL TELEMETRY

paragraphsHtml: At the wire level, Semantic governance policies interpose between the model and your agent runtime rather than between the agent and downstream tools. When you route agent model egress through Agent Gateway, every non-streamed model response containing a proposed tool call is forwarded to the policy engine before reaching your agent process. An LLM judge evaluates the call against the full conversation history, the agent’s system instructions (where time-sensitive facts such as earnings dates must reside), tool descriptions, and attached natural-language policies.

If both checks pass—user intent alignment and explicit policy rules—the original model response passes to your agent untouched. If either check fails, the engine strips the proposed tool calls and substitutes your configured --agent-response-denial-message (preventing internal compliance wording from leaking to end users), while writing the verdict, judge rationale, and evaluation token count to Cloud Logging. In Google’s finance walkthrough, an authorized send to controller@example.com passed, an NDA-justified send to jordan@investor.example was blocked entirely by policy, and an injected delete_file call from a planning doc was stopped by the built-in intent check.

To catch cross-turn behavioral drift that looks valid one call at a time—such as paging list_inventory in batches of 100 across an entire catalog—Agent Anomaly Detection reads OpenTelemetry spans and conversation events shipped to telemetry.googleapis.com. Setting OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=EVENT_ONLY and ADK_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT_IN_SPANS=false keeps payloads structured for analysis, surfacing external agents in the Monitored agents list within 30 minutes and flagging real failures such as 10 of 40 runaway Amazon Nova Lite Bedrock sessions and 4 of 6 Microsoft Foundry refund-override exploits.

faqPlain.question: Does Semantic governance work if our agents call Claude, OpenAI-compatible, or self-hosted vLLM models?
faqPlain.answer: Yes. Agent Gateway evaluates proposed tool calls regardless of whether your agent reaches Gemini API, Anthropic Messages API, Claude models on Gemini platform, or OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoints including self-hosted vLLM servers.

faqPlain.question: Do we have to migrate AWS Bedrock or Azure Foundry workloads to GCP to use Agent Anomaly Detection?
faqPlain.answer: No. Agents remain on AWS Lambda, Microsoft Foundry, or on-premises infrastructure. Using keyless Workload Identity Federation and ADK Python v2.12.0+ OpenTelemetry exporters, only telemetry traces and message-content logs travel to telemetry.googleapis.com.

faqPlain.question: What happens to normal conversational answers when Semantic governance is enabled?
faqPlain.answer: Responses that contain only text—such as an explanation, plan, or clarifying question—skip the policy engine completely because they invoke no tool action. Only responses proposing tool calls undergo policy and user-intent evaluation.
